implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Provides the navigation header for the event management suite, showing 'Event Manager' as logo, with links to All Events and New Event, and highlighting the active link based on the current request path.
implementation.name: Header Navigation (All Events, New Event)
implementation.pseudo_code:
Render header with:
  - Logo linking to root_path labelled 'Event Manager'
  - Navigation links:
      - All Events (active if request.path == events_path OR root_path)
      - New Event (active if request.path == new_event_path)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Renders breadcrumbs for navigation context beneath the header, showing the user's current location within the event management suite with clickable parent segments.
implementation.name: Breadcrumbs
implementation.pseudo_code:
Render breadcrumb list:
  Always show: Home (link to root_path)
  IF request.path != root_path AND request.path != events_path:
    Show: Events (link to events_path)
  IF path includes '/events/new':
    Show: New Event (current, non-clickable)
  ELSE IF path matches /events/:id/edit:
    Show: @event.title (link to event_path(@event))
    Show: Edit (current, non-clickable)
  ELSE IF path matches /events/:id (not edit):
    Show: @event.title (current, non-clickable)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Displays all events sorted by newest first, with each item showing title, description (or 'No description'), assigned user count badge, and actions: View, Edit, Remove (with confirm dialog). Shows empty state message with link to create first event when no events exist.
implementation.name: Event List UI
implementation.pseudo_code:
Render 'Add New Event' button linking to new_event_path
Render event-list:
  FOR each event in @events:
    Show event title
    IF event.assigned_user_count > 0:
      Show user count badge (e.g. '3 users')
    Show event.description OR 'No description'
    Show actions:

      Edit (link to edit_event_path)
      Remove (form with DELETE method, onsubmit confirm dialog)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Shared form partial for creating and editing events. Renders title and description fields, a user assignment section with searchable multi-select checkboxes loaded from @users, a selection counter, and Save/Cancel buttons. Inline JavaScript handles live search filtering and selected user count updates.
implementation.name: Event Form UI (New/Edit)
implementation.pseudo_code:
Render form_with model: event:
  IF event.errors present:
    Show error messages in alert div
  Field: title (text_field, required)
  Field: description (text_area, optional)
  Field: Assign Users:
    Hidden field for empty assignment submission
    User assignment container:
      Search input (#user-search)
      User list:
        IF @users present:
          FOR each user:
            Checkbox (event[assigned_user_ids][]) with user id
            Pre-check IF user id in event.assigned_user_ids
            Show user name and email
        ELSE:
          Show 'Loading users...'
      Selected count display (#selected-count)
  Actions:
    Submit button
    Cancel link to events_path
Inline JS on DOMContentLoaded:
  updateSelectedCount(): count checked .user-checkbox, update #selected-count
  filterUsers(): on search input, show/hide .user-checkbox-item by name/email match
  Bind: searchInput on input -> filterUsers
  Bind: each checkbox on change -> updateSelectedCount
  Call updateSelectedCount() on load

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Defines RESTful routes for all event management actions and sets events#index as the root route.
implementation.name: resources :events
implementation.pseudo_code:
root -> events#index
GET    /events          -> events#index
GET    /events/new      -> events#new
POST   /events          -> events#create
GET    /events/:id      -> events#show
GET    /events/:id/edit -> events#edit
PATCH  /events/:id      -> events#update
PUT    /events/:id      -> events#update
DELETE /events/:id      -> events#destroy

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Handles event creation including user assignment. On success, redirects to the new event's show page with a green success notice. On failure, reloads @users and re-renders the new form with validation errors.

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Fetches the full external user list from JSONPlaceholder API with a 5-minute Rails cache. Used to populate the user assignment checkboxes in the event form.
implementation.name: JsonplaceholderService.fetch_users
implementation.pseudo_code:
Check Rails.cache for 'jsonplaceholder_users' (expires_in: 5 minutes):
  IF cache miss:
    GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users
    IF response.code == '200':
      Parse and return JSON user array
    ELSE:
      Return []
    IF exception:
      Log error
      Return []
  ELSE:
    Return cached user list

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Fetches a single user by ID from the JSONPlaceholder API with a 5-minute Rails cache per user. Used by Event#assigned_users to resolve each assigned user ID into a full user object for display in the event detail view.
implementation.name: JsonplaceholderService.fetch_user
implementation.pseudo_code:
Check Rails.cache for 'jsonplaceholder_user_<user_id>' (expires_in: 5 minutes):
  IF cache miss:
    GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/<user_id>
    IF response.code == '200':
      Parse and return JSON user object
    ELSE:
      Return nil
    IF exception:
      Log error
      Return nil
  ELSE:
    Return cached user object

missing_implementations: Event removal via list/detail prompts for confirmation; upon confirming, deletes event, returns to list view, and displays status message (green or red based on outcome). The destroy action in EventsController always redirects with a success notice and has no begin/rescue block to catch failures, so a red error alert message is never shown to the user when the destroy operation fails.
